an7.70:4.1: “Sir, as I was in private retreat this thought came to my mind,
an7.70:4.2: ‘What should a mendicant honor and respect and rely on, to give up the unskillful and develop the skillful?’
an7.70:4.4: ‘A mendicant should honor and respect and rely on the Teacher, to give up the unskillful and develop the skillful.
an7.70:4.5: A mendicant should honor and respect and rely on the teaching …
an7.70:4.6: A mendicant should honor and respect and rely on hospitality …
an7.70:4.9: ‘These qualities are pure and bright in me. Why don’t I go and tell them to the Buddha?
an7.70:4.10: Then these qualities will not only be purified in me, but will be better known as purified.
an7.70:4.11: Suppose a man were to acquire a gold ingot, pure and bright.
an7.70:4.13: My gold ingot is pure and bright. Why don’t I take it to show the smiths?
an7.70:4.14: Then it will not only be purified, but will be better known as purified.
an7.70:4.15: In the same way, these qualities are pure and bright in me. Why don’t I go and tell them to the Buddha?
an7.70:4.16: Then these qualities will not only be purified in me, but will be better known as purified.’”
an7.70:13.1: It is quite impossible for a mendicant who does respect the Teacher … and diligence to disrespect hospitality.
an7.70:15.1: It’s quite possible for a mendicant who respects the Teacher … and diligence to respect hospitality.
an7.70:17.4: A mendicant who disrespects the Teacher, the teaching, the Saṅgha, the training, and immersion disrespects diligence.
an7.70:18.1: It is quite impossible for a mendicant who doesn’t respect the Teacher, the teaching, the Saṅgha, the training, immersion, and diligence to respect hospitality.
an7.70:20.1: It is quite impossible for a mendicant who does respect the Teacher, the teaching … and diligence to disrespect hospitality.
an7.70:22.1: It’s quite possible for a mendicant who respects the Teacher … and diligence to respect hospitality.
